title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 57–59, 'Ateliers', July 1986): Grothendieck works with sets E carrying a symmetric relation |∘|_E. The relation is anti-reflexive, or, in a variant, a point related to itself is related to every point, like a null element. On p. 57 a morphism E → E' is a correspondence α: E → 𝔓(E') that is compatible with the relations: for all x, y in E, if x |∘| y then x' |∘| y' for every x' ∈ α(x) and y' ∈ α(y). Composition is the usual composition of correspondences, (βα)(x) = ⋃_{x'∈α(x)} β(x').

On this page he states:
(1) These data form a category. Its objects are 'the same as' strict (simple, loopless) graphs.
(2) He proposes names: a set with such a relation is a 'disposition' (ensemble muni d'une relation de disposition). Morphisms are 'morphismes de dispositions', written dis(E, E'), and there is a 'catégorie des dispositions'.
(3) For a morphism α he extends it by unions to ᾱ: 𝔓(E) → 𝔓(E'), A ↦ ⋃_{x∈A} α(x).
(4) He defines α_*: Σ_E → Σ_{E'} as the composite Σ_E ⊂ 𝔓(E) → 𝔓(E') → Σ_{E'}, i.e. α_*(S) = supp°_{E'}(ᾱ(S)). Here Σ_E is the set of 'closed' subsets ('spatios', p. 57). supp° is a closure operator built from |∘|; most plausibly the biorthogonal (Galois/polarity) closure A ↦ A^{∘∘}, where A^∘ = {x : x |∘| a for all a ∈ A}.
(5) He remarks (p. 59) that α_* is defined whether or not α is compatible.

Modern reading: these are orthogonality spaces (Dacey 1968; Foulis–Randall). Σ_E is then the complete ortholattice of biorthogonally closed subsets, and Grothendieck is trying to make E ↦ Σ_E functorial for relation-preserving correspondences. The purpose, from p. 57, is to get convenient 'spaces' Σ on which to formulate axioms for his '∘-structures' in the Ateliers chapter.

The key formula he then wants (p. 59) is α_*(supp° A) = supp°(ᾱ(A)). With it, α_* would be well behaved and composition would be preserved. He crosses out his attempted proof and writes that it 'must be false'.
errors: Calling the objects 'equivalent to strict graphs' is right at the level of objects. The category is not the usual category of graphs, though, because morphisms are relation-preserving multivalued correspondences rather than vertex maps.
If supp° is the biorthogonal closure, compatibility only gives ᾱ(A^∘) ⊆ ᾱ(A)^∘. This does not yield ᾱ(A^∘∘) ⊆ ᾱ(A)^∘∘, so the formula hoped for on p. 59 fails in general.

Counterexample to that formula. Take E = {a,b,c} with a⊥c and b⊥c, so {a}^⊥⊥ = {a,b}. Take E' = {a',b',c',d'} with a'⊥c', b'⊥c' and a'⊥d'. Let α send a, b, c to a', b', c'; this α is compatible. Then α_*({a}^⊥⊥) = cl{a',b'} = {a',b'}, whereas cl(ᾱ{a}) = cl{a'} = {a'}.
Consequently α ↦ α_* need not be a functor on the category of dispositions without extra hypotheses. Grothendieck's own doubt on p. 59 ('ça doit être faux') is justified.

ideas.what: Category of sets with a symmetric (irreflexive) relation, with morphisms being relation-preserving correspondences E → 𝔓(E'), named 'dispositions'
ideas.modern_name: orthogonality spaces (orthosets) with relational / multivalued morphisms; simple graphs with a relational-morphism category
ideas.usually_credited_to: Dacey (1968), Foulis–Randall (1970s); categorical treatments by Moore, Hartonas, Paseka–Vetterlein (2010s–2020s)

ideas.what: Extension of a correspondence to power sets by unions, composed with a closure operator to give α_*: Σ_E → Σ_{E'} between lattices of closed subsets
ideas.modern_name: induced map on biorthogonally closed sets / Galois-closed sets (polarities); attempt to make E ↦ C(E) a functor

missed.claim: In 1986, apparently independently, Grothendieck sets up the framework of orthogonality spaces from the quantum-logic tradition. This is a set with a symmetric irreflexive relation, the lattice Σ_E of closed subsets, and relation-preserving correspondences as morphisms. He also runs into the known obstacle that the induced maps on closed subsets are not functorial in general. Neither the quantum-logic literature nor the Grothendieck literature seems to record the link.
missed.quote: On pourrait appeler un (E, |∘|_E) un ensemble muni d'une relation de disposition, ou disposition
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical. It shows Grothendieck's late 'Ateliers' foundations moving toward orthoset / ortholattice ideas, which are actively studied today (e.g. Paseka–Vetterlein on categories of orthosets). It adds nothing new mathematically.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine definitions: a category of graphs/orthosets with relational morphisms and an induced map on closed sets. The only point of interest is historical, namely the unacknowledged overlap with orthogonality-space theory and the functoriality problem he hits on p. 59.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: the struck-through words are 'la catégorie', and the category symbol after them is unclear (transcribed 'E𝒱').
The relation symbol is |∘|_E, as on p. 57, not '𝒱_E'.
Third arrow in the composite and in the definition of α_*: the label reads 'suppr°_{E'}' or 'supp°_{E'}'. Page 59 has 'supp⁰', so this is probably supp°.
The struck-out symbol before ᾱ is 'Σ_E' over a scribble.
Last line: 'Cette application est en fait définie quelle que soit…'. The struck word is 'sur'/'quelque', replaced by 'quelle'; it continues on p. 59 with 'que soit la correspondance α'.
In the definition of ᾱ, the union index is x ∈ A.
